answer: Bond each new identity with a stake that vests one slice per epoch, and release payouts only when an established peer co-signs and shares the slashing risk. A sybil farm must lock N bonds up front and wait through N slow releases, so its return per fake stays linear, never better than simply running one honest identity. Fake networks are karst: hard crust, hollow beneath, collapsing the moment anyone drills. Let reputation grow like a willow instead, deep roots and cheap branches, so every identity is paid for before its fable is believed.
